idiom_name: Vapor Queues maxRetryCount + Job.error hook writing into a durable dead-letter store (or a DLT topic via swift-kafka-client)
implementation_notes: Nothing in the Swift server stack provides a dead-letter channel, so it is assembled from the retry primitive and the hook that survives it: Vapor Queues (NIO-backed workers, Redis or database driver) retries a job up to maxRetryCount and then calls the job's error(_:error:_:) method, which is the only place that still owns both the payload and the thrown error when the budget is spent. The dead-letter write belongs there - a failed_jobs row in the same database (or a dead-letter topic produced through swift-server/swift-kafka-client for log-based transports) carrying the payload, the error and the attempt count, plus an operator path to retry or discard. Doing nothing in the hook, or logging only, is the Swift-shaped version of silently dropping the message.
pitfalls: error(_:error:_:) is called for every failed attempt, not only the last one: writing to the dead-letter store there without checking the attempt count parks each transient retry.

A throw inside the error hook is swallowed by the driver, so the dead-letter write must not throw on transient database errors without its own retry, and the payload must be Codable to be rebuildable later.

Retry bookkeeping lives in the driver (Redis or the database): a worker crash or a lost reservation can re-run a job whose dead-letter record already exists - dedupe on job id or a natural idempotency key.
Doing blocking work in the hook occupies an EventLoop thread and stalls other jobs on the same loop; database writes must go through the async/NIO path.
